assumptions: Freshness = clone HEAD equals `git ls-remote origin HEAD` (human-settled fork); FETCH_HEAD mtime is no longer read anywhere in the session siren.

ls-remote is bounded by a bash watchdog (macOS ships no `timeout`); default 3s, overridable via CANARY_SIREN_LS_REMOTE_TIMEOUT. A timeout is told apart from a git failure by whether the watchdog fired, since git's own exit 128 overlaps signal codes.

Failed, timed-out, or empty (no HEAD) ls-remote yields one explicit 'unverifiable' finding covering both clone freshness and installed-plugin staleness; check 4b then stays quiet rather than duplicating it.

Clone-behind remedy is `git -C '<clone>' pull --ff-only` (verified by a test that runs it verbatim and re-runs the siren). `claude plugin marketplace update` is no longer named because its effect on the clone cannot be tested here.

Check 4b now compares the installed gitCommitSha against origin's live HEAD rather than @{upstream}/origin/HEAD; its remedy is prefixed 'once the clone is at origin' because reinstall copies from the clone.
GIT_SSH_COMMAND is not overridden (would clobber a user's core.sshCommand); GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and stdin </dev/null plus the timeout bound any prompt.
No other copies of the hook exist: scripts/install-siren.mjs symlinks hooks/canary-session-siren.sh; .claude-plugin/hooks.json does not ship it.
